Maps Dorado split-read identifiers back to their original POD5 parents using explicitly provided SAM/BAM tags. Returns the signal for the corresponding basecalled interval in acquisition order.

Source: R/extract_pod5_signal_dorado.R
extract_pod5_signal_dorado.Rd

Dorado assigns new UUIDs to split-read children, which are generally not present in the original POD5 file. The parent read is identified by pi. Using zero-based coordinates, the requested interval starts at sp + ts and ends immediately before sp + ns. Its length is therefore ns - ts, rather than ns.

Usage

extract_pod5_signal_dorado(file, reads, calibrated = FALSE)

Arguments

file

character or external pointer. Path to the original POD5 file, or an open reader.

reads

Data frame. Columns read_id, pi, sp, ts, and ns are required. read_id contains unique Dorado query-name UUIDs, while pi contains parent UUIDs or missing values for unsplit reads. Numeric sp, ts, and ns contain the corresponding Dorado SAM/BAM tag values. Missing sp is permitted only when no parent is specified; ts and ns must always be present.

calibrated

logical Defaults to FALSE. Return picoamperes instead of ADC counts.

Value

A list named by canonical lowercase Dorado read UUIDs, preserving input row order. Raw signal vectors are integer; calibrated vectors are numeric. Empty intervals return empty vectors of the corresponding type.

Details

Under the current Dorado SAM specification, ns is the end coordinate after any rear trimming and does not necessarily represent the full untrimmed child. Do not add the acquisition-level POD5 start_sample to these offsets.

For unsplit reads, set pi to NA_character_ or an empty string, and sp to NA_real_ or zero. In that case, the POD5 identifier is read_id; the interval starts at ts and ends immediately before ns. A pi value equal to read_id with sp = 0 is also accepted.

It does not parse BAM files, infer missing tags, reverse RNA or reverse-strand signals, or support duplex consensus reads. If present, dx must contain only -1 or 0; duplex records with value 1 are rejected. Supply one row per read rather than repeated alignment records. A child UUID alone, or a parent identifier without sample offsets, is insufficient to recover a split-read interval.

See also

extract_pod5_signal, read_pod5, and https://software-docs.nanoporetech.com/dorado/latest/basecaller/sam_spec/

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# reads contains read_id plus pi, sp, ts, and ns tags obtained from Dorado BAM
signals <- pod5R::extract_pod5_signal_dorado("reads.pod5", reads)
} # }
